finding: Among patients taking antihypertensives in the Arizona desert, 40.5% of syncope cases in summer were caused by dehydration, against 29% in winter (p = 0.04). The type of antihypertensive made no difference.

finding: Irbesartan with hydrochlorothiazide lowered systolic blood pressure 3.9 mmHg less at 8 weeks when started in spring or summer than when started in autumn or winter (501 patients, China).

finding: In lithium users, higher temperature on the day of testing trended toward a lower dose-to-level ratio (beta -0.17, p = 0.08). The authors judged it of little clinical importance in temperate climates and called for study above 40 °C.
